# Region Sjælland — Sjælland

Region Sjælland (the administrative healthcare organization) and Sjælland (the geographical and statistical region) are deeply intertwined entities within the Danish healthcare system. Both are integral to the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] and are continuously evaluated in national quality reports for [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation). While "Sjælland" refers to the physical and demographic territory—one of the five primary subdivisions of [[danmark|Danmark]] [^src19] [^src23] [^src25]—"Region Sjælland" is the organizational body responsible for healthcare delivery, data reporting, and clinical performance within that territory. 

Geographically and organizationally, the region encompasses a wide network of medical facilities. It contains several major hospitals, including [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]], [[holbaek|Holbæk]], [[nykoebing-falster|Nykøbing Falster]], [[naestved-sygehus|Næstved]], [[sjaellands-universitetshospital-koenge|Sjællands Universitetshospital Køge]], [[sjaellands-universitetshospital-roskilde|Sjællands Universitetshospital Roskilde]], and [[slagelse-sygehus|Slagelse]] [^src14]. Furthermore, the region's healthcare infrastructure is organized into localized health clusters, notably [[sundhedsklyngen-holbaek|Sundhedsklyngen Holbæk]], [[sundhedsklyngen-nykoebing-f|Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F]], and [[sundhedsklyngen-slagelse|Sundhedsklyngen Slagelse]] [^src25]. 

The clinical performance of Region Sjælland is tracked across multiple national indicators. For Indikator 1, Sjælland achieved a result of 90.6% (95% CI: 89.2–91.9) in the 2022–2023 period [^src10], and 90.9% in a subsequent reporting period [^src5]. Across all regions, the proportion varied between 91% and 93%, meaning the standard was met universally for this metric [^src5]. However, performance dips below the [[standard-80-percent|Standard: ≥80 %]] for [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]]. In Region Sjælland, this indicator was fulfilled by 75.9% (95% CI: 74.2–77.6) of newly diagnosed patients [^src11], and later recorded at 78.0% [^src6]. The eastern regions, including Sjælland, consistently fell slightly below the 80% threshold compared to their western counterparts [^src6]. For [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]], no regions in Denmark meet the standard, with proportions varying between 71% and 82% [^src12]. 

Region Sjælland also struggles with [[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]] and [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]. The organization does not meet the standard for Indikator 4b, scoring in the 92–94% range [^src1], and no health clusters in the eastern regions meet this standard either [^src27]. For Indikator 5, Region Sjælland recorded an incidence of 1.0% (95% CI: 0.9–1.1) [^src1] and later 0.9% (95% CI: 0.8–1.0) [^src27], failing to meet the required >0.8% standard. Regionally, the incidence of atrial fibrillation was notably higher in [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] and Sjælland (0.9–1.0%) than in the three other Danish regions (0.7%) [^src16]. Overall, the national incidence of atrial fibrillation was recorded at 3.3 per 1,000 inhabitants [^src2], while regional mortality varied between 7.4% and 7.9% [^src22].

Beyond clinical outcomes, the region exhibits specific operational patterns. The laboratory code [[npu04998-p-creatinin|NPU04998]] for p-creatinin measurements is predominantly used in Region Hovedstaden and Region Sjælland [^src27]. Despite its active participation in the national registry, when asked for qualitative feedback, Region Sjælland provided "Ingen kommentarer" (No comments) to the database administrators [^src4] [^src9].
